records.title: Reward points migration on card variant upgrade is currently a manual Ops process
records.summary: Today, when a customer moves to a higher credit card variant, Ops manually debits their reward points balance on the old card and credits it to the new card using a conversion ratio. There is no automated platform handling of this.

records.title: Build a generalized platform feature for reward migration on card upgrade or downgrade, not a per-case fix
records.summary: Chose to pursue a platform feature that automates reward point migration for any credit card variant change — upgrade or downgrade — rather than continuing the current manual, Ops-driven, per-case process.

alternatives_considered.option: Continue current manual Ops process (debit old card, credit new card per conversion ratio, handled case-by-case)
cons: Doesn't scale across all card variant pairs
Ops-dependent for every upgrade or downgrade
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: User wants a platform capability that works for any credit card variant change, not a per-pair manual workaround.

alternatives_considered.option: Build a generalized platform feature that automates reward migration for any credit card upgrade or downgrade
pros: Scales to any card variant pair, either direction, without new Ops work per pair
Removes manual handling and its error surface
cons: Requires defining conversion ratio logic generically across all variant pairs and both directions
Scope and edge cases not yet fully known

data.recommendation: Build a platform feature that automates reward point migration for any credit card variant change, upgrade or downgrade, replacing the manual Ops process.
data.rationale: The user explicitly stated the goal is a platform feature that works for any credit card upgrade, and confirmed downgrade is in scope too — not a one-off fix for a single card pair or direction, to remove Ops from the manual debit/credit loop.

records.title: Initiative is on the platform roadmap; driven by Ops not scaling with upgrade/downgrade volume
records.summary: This feature is a committed platform roadmap item. The stated driver is that Ops cannot keep up with the manual debit/credit process as the volume of card variant upgrades/downgrades grows with scale.

records.title: Current manual migration volume is ~500/month, expected to grow into the thousands
records.summary: Ops currently processes roughly 500 card upgrade/downgrade reward point migrations manually per month. Volume is expected to grow into the thousands as the platform scales, which Ops cannot handle manually at that level.

records.title: Conversion ratio/method is defined per client, not fixed platform-wide
records.summary: Each client (e.g. a bank) defines the points conversion approach for its own card variant pairs. Cited examples: a fixed percentage ratio (e.g. 70%), keeping point count equal, and keeping point value equal. The feature must support all of these as client-configurable options, not a single hardcoded formula.

records.title: The three anticipated conversion methods cover clients' real needs
records.summary: The three conversion approaches described (fixed percentage, equal point count, equal point value) are anticipated by the user, not confirmed against actual client requirements. No client has yet validated that these are the only methods they need.

data.statement: Clients' points-conversion requirements on card upgrade/downgrade will be fully covered by fixed-percentage, equal-point-count, and equal-point-value methods.
data.impact_if_wrong: If real client requirements include a different conversion method (e.g. tiered/graduated ratios, minimum point guarantees, promotional overrides), the platform feature's configuration model may need rework before or during client onboarding.

records.title: Card variant change is already published as an event by an internal system
records.summary: When a customer's card variant changes (upgrade or downgrade), an internal system already publishes an event for it. The platform feature can react to this existing event rather than needing to detect the card variant change itself.

records.title: Primary success criterion: exact points reconciliation per client's chosen method
records.summary: The stated measure of success for this feature is that reward points reconcile exactly according to whichever conversion method the client has configured (fixed percentage, equal count, or equal value) — no discrepancy between what should be credited/debited and what actually is.

records.title: Customer disputes over migrated point amount
records.summary: The primary risk identified is a customer disputing the number of reward points they receive after a card variant migration. Reward points carry real value to customers, so an incorrect or unclear migration amount is expected to surface as a dispute.

records.title: Partial/failed migration is not seen as a significant concern
records.summary: The user does not consider a migration failing partway (customer left without correct old-card debit or new-card credit) to be a significant risk here, distinct from the customer-dispute risk already identified.

records.title: Same-day processing is an acceptable latency for migration
records.summary: Points migration does not need to happen in real time. Completing within the same business day the card-variant-change event fires is acceptable.

records.title: Feature scope covers both upgrade and downgrade
records.summary: Confirmed the platform feature must support reward point migration in both directions: when a customer upgrades to a higher card variant and when a customer downgrades to a lower one.

records.title: Migration is triggered automatically by the existing card-variant-change event
records.summary: The platform automatically initiates a reward points migration whenever the existing card-variant-change event fires, for both upgrades and downgrades, with no manual Ops step.

data.statement: The system automatically initiates a reward points migration whenever the existing card-variant-change event fires, for both upgrades and downgrades, without requiring manual Ops action.
acceptance_criteria: When the internal system publishes a card-variant-change event for a customer (upgrade or downgrade), the platform initiates a points migration for that customer without any manual Ops step.
Every published card-variant-change event results in either a completed migration or a flagged failure requiring review — none are silently dropped.
edge_cases: (solution-design's judgment, not evidence) If a card-variant-change event references a card variant pair with no conversion method configured by the client, the migration is not silently skipped or defaulted — it is flagged for manual review, since guessing a method would contradict the exact-reconciliation success criterion in insight-2026-08-10-success-criteria-reconciliation.

records.details: Implements the core of decision-2026-08-10-generalized-platform-feature's recommendation to replace the manual Ops process (insight-2026-08-10-manual-points-migration) by reacting to the event already published today (insight-2026-08-10-existing-trigger-event). This automation is what addresses the scaling concern raised in insight-2026-08-10-roadmap-and-scaling-driver and insight-2026-08-10-migration-volume (~500/month today, expected to grow into the thousands).

records.title: Conversion method is configurable per client, per card variant pair
records.summary: Each client configures which conversion method applies to a given card variant pair — fixed percentage, equal point count, or equal point value — and migrations apply whichever method is configured for that specific pair.

data.statement: For each card variant pair, the client configures which conversion method applies — fixed percentage, equal point count, or equal point value — and the migration applies whichever method is configured for that exact pair.
acceptance_criteria: A client can configure, per card variant pair, exactly one method: a fixed conversion percentage, an equal-point-count method, or an equal-point-value method.
When a migration runs for a given card variant pair, it applies the method configured for that exact pair rather than a platform-wide default.
Two different clients can configure different conversion methods for otherwise-identical card variant pairs without one client's configuration affecting the other's.

records.details: Carries forward the caveat in assumption-2026-08-10-conversion-methods-exhaustive: the three methods implemented here (fixed percentage, equal point count, equal point value) are anticipated by the user, not yet validated against real client requirements (insight-2026-08-10-client-defined-conversion-ratio). If a client's real requirement doesn't fit one of these three methods, this requirement will need to be revisited — that gap is not resolved here, only built as currently scoped.

records.title: Migrated point balance reconciles exactly to the configured conversion method
records.summary: After a migration completes, the old card's full point balance is debited and the new card is credited with exactly the value the configured conversion method computes from it — no discrepancy.

data.statement: After a migration completes, the points debited from the old card equal its full pre-migration balance, and the points credited to the new card equal exactly the value the client's configured conversion method computes from that debited amount.
acceptance_criteria: The old card's point balance after migration is zero (its full pre-migration balance was debited).

The new card's credited amount matches the value computed by applying the configured conversion method to the debited amount, with no rounding or calculation discrepancy beyond the method's defined precision.
Given the same starting balance and the same configured method, repeating the calculation produces the identical credited amount every time.

records.details: Directly implements the success criterion captured in insight-2026-08-10-success-criteria-reconciliation: exact reconciliation per the client's chosen method. Exactness here is what determines whether risk-2026-08-10-customer-dispute materializes, since a mismatch between the expected and received amount is the disputed condition itself.

records.title: Migration completes within the same business day as the triggering event
records.summary: Every points migration completes within the same business day the triggering card-variant-change event was published; real-time processing is not required.

data.statement: Every points migration completes within the same business day the triggering card-variant-change event was published.
acceptance_criteria: For a card-variant-change event published on a given business day, the corresponding migration (old card debited, new card credited) completes before that business day ends.
Migration is not required to complete in real time or within minutes of the event; same-business-day completion satisfies this requirement.
edge_cases: (solution-design's judgment, not evidence) An event published outside business hours or on a non-business day is processed by the end of the next business day, since same-day completion has no defined meaning outside a business day.

records.details: Implements insight-2026-08-10-same-day-sla, which established that real-time processing is not required.

records.title: Every migration produces a retrievable audit record for dispute investigation
records.summary: Every completed migration produces a retrievable record of the old balance, new balance, conversion method applied, and timestamp, sufficient to investigate a customer's dispute about the amount they received.

data.statement: Every points migration produces a retrievable record of the pre-migration balance, post-migration balance, the specific conversion method and parameters applied, and the completion timestamp.
acceptance_criteria: For any completed migration, the pre-migration balance, post-migration balance, the conversion method and parameters applied (e.g. which percentage, or which method type), and the completion timestamp can be retrieved by card or customer identifier.
The audit record is created and retained at migration time, independent of whether a dispute is ever raised — not generated on-demand only after a dispute occurs.

records.details: (solution-design's judgment, not evidence) risk-2026-08-10-customer-dispute identifies customer disputes over the migrated amount as the primary risk. Resolving a dispute requires being able to show what happened and why; without a retrievable per-migration record, a dispute can only be asserted, not investigated. This requirement doesn't attempt to prevent disputes — that's what requirement-2026-08-10-exact-points-reconciliation targets — it makes disputes that do occur investigable.

records.title: No existing way to detect a card-variant-change event that produced neither a migration nor a flagged failure
records.summary: The requirement that every published event result in a completed migration or a flagged failure depends on being able to prove that outcome — a capability the platform doesn't have today.

data.impact_description: A card-variant-change event that fails before migration processing even starts (consumer outage, dropped message) looks identical to a day with no card variant changes at all, unless the platform tracks event-received counts against migration-completed-or-flagged counts and alerts on any gap — that comparison doesn't exist today because Ops previously processed each case by hand and would notice via a customer calling in, not a systemic count mismatch.

records.title: Missing per-pair conversion configuration creates a new Ops exception queue
records.summary: When a card variant pair has no conversion method configured, the migration is flagged for manual review — turning Ops from processing every migration into triaging an exception queue that doesn't exist as a workflow today.

data.impact_description: Today Ops manually processes every migration, so there's no separate 'missing configuration' failure mode to route anywhere. Once migration is automated, any card variant pair a client hasn't configured a method for (e.g., a newly launched variant) falls into a flagged-for-review state with no defined owner, queue, or SLA of its own — distinct from the general migration process it's replacing.

records.title: New per-client, per-card-variant-pair conversion configuration storage doesn't exist yet
records.summary: Which of the three methods, with which parameters, applies to a given card variant pair for a given client is a new configuration entity the platform has no data model for today.

data.impact_description: Storing 'which method (fixed percentage / equal count / equal value), with which parameters (e.g., which percentage), applies to card variant pair X for client Y' is new structured configuration — today this exists only as a person's judgment call per manual case, not as a queryable data model the automated migration can look up per pair per client.

records.title: Fixed-percentage conversion can produce fractional point amounts with no defined precision rule
records.summary: A fixed-percentage method applied to an arbitrary balance will often produce a non-integer result, but the platform has no defined rounding/precision rule to make 'exact' well-defined in that case.

data.impact_description: A fixed-percentage method (e.g. 70%) applied to an arbitrary pre-migration balance often produces a non-integer result (e.g. 233 points at 70% = 163.1), but the acceptance criterion demands crediting 'exactly the value...with no rounding or calculation discrepancy beyond the method's defined precision' — no precision or rounding rule is defined anywhere in the requirements or the existing points ledger, so 'exact' is currently undefined for any non-whole-number outcome.

records.title: No existing way to see which migrations are approaching the same-day SLA before it's breached
records.summary: Batched, same-business-day processing needs a way to tell 'still within today's window' apart from 'about to breach the deadline,' which the platform has no metric for today.

data.impact_description: Because migration is asynchronous and completes any time within a business day rather than immediately per event, the platform needs to distinguish a migration still within today's processing window from one about to breach the same-day deadline — a pending-migration age metric that doesn't exist today since Ops closed each case synchronously by hand as it came in.

records.title: Migration audit record is a new data entity distinct from the points ledger
records.summary: Capturing and retaining the conversion method and parameters applied per migration is metadata a balance-tracking ledger entry doesn't inherently carry, so a new retained record type is needed.

data.impact_description: The audit requirement needs the specific conversion method and parameters applied (e.g. which percentage) captured per migration and retained regardless of whether a dispute occurs — that's metadata about how a balance change was computed, which a balance-tracking points ledger transaction entry doesn't inherently carry, so a new record type keyed by migration (not just a ledger line item) needs to exist.

records.title: Audit record being retrievable doesn't mean the support agent fielding a dispute can reach it
records.summary: The requirement guarantees the record is retrievable by identifier, but not who can retrieve it — support agents have no defined access path today, unlike Ops who had direct system access during the manual process.

data.impact_description: The requirement guarantees the pre/post balance, method, and timestamp are retrievable by card or customer identifier, but says nothing about who can retrieve them. Today a dispute over a manual migration would be resolved by Ops, who performed the migration and had direct system access; once migration is automated, the customer support agent who actually fields the dispute call has no defined tool or permission path to look up that record unless one is built, leaving the data retrievable in principle but not by the people who need it to answer a customer in the moment.

records.title: Automating migration removes the only point where a customer might currently learn their points changed
records.summary: None of the five requirements specify telling the customer when a migration completes, and automation removes the one human touchpoint the manual process had.

data.impact_description: None of the five requirements specify notifying the customer when a migration completes. The manual Ops process at least involved a person touching the account on the day of the change; full automation removes that without replacing it with any customer-facing signal, so a customer's points balance changing via an unannounced automated debit-then-credit is exactly the condition risk-2026-08-10-customer-dispute already identifies as the primary risk — this gap is a direct driver of that risk's likelihood, independent of whether the calculation itself is correct.

records.title: Undefined rounding direction on fractional point conversions could create a systematic, portfolio-level point-liability discrepancy
records.summary: If the platform's rounding rule for fixed-percentage conversions consistently rounds one direction, the effect compounds across the full migration volume into an aggregate accounting discrepancy, distinct from any single customer's dispute.
records.details: Surfaced while assessing system-impact-2026-08-10-conversion-rounding-precision: requirement-2026-08-10-exact-points-reconciliation defines exactness per-migration but says nothing about aggregate drift across migrations, and no rounding direction is specified anywhere in the requirements to date. At current/projected volume (insight-2026-08-10-migration-volume: ~500/month growing into the thousands), a one-directional rounding rule would compound into a portfolio-level point-liability discrepancy between what the client's conversion formula specifies and what the platform actually issues — a finance/accounting exposure separate from any individual customer's dispute over their own amount. This is distinct from insight-2026-08-10-no-partial-failure-concern (which addresses per-customer partial-failure, not aggregate accounting drift) and from risk-2026-08-10-customer-dispute (which is about individual disputed amounts, not portfolio-level totals).
